source.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models
source.authors: Naiyu Yin; Dennis Wei; Tian Gao; Amit Dhurandhar; K. Ramamurthy; Yue Yu

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes relationships among SAE features across model layers, but does not test dictionary-size splitting, feature coverage, directional proximity, or the other claim versions. Its use of pre-trained SAEs is not a use of the splitting finding.
record.gate_note: The GPT-2 small case study reports qualitative semantic relationships among layer-wise SAE features; these bear on the general subject of feature relationships but do not test any listed version. The study does not vary SAE dictionary size or measure split-feature input coverage or geometric proximity. Circuit benchmark accuracy/runtime, circuit ablations, and domain-generalization results concern other outcomes and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a Lasso-based circuit-discovery method and applies it to pre-trained SAE features at one fixed dictionary size per model. It never varies SAE size or sparsity, and it never measures whether coarse features split into finer ones, whether children cover a parent's inputs, or how close they lie in direction. It also does not measure absorption, latent decomposition across sizes, or objective-dependence. Its cross-layer persistence, merging and dropping observations concern feature flow between layers, not feature splitting within a growing dictionary. The only contact with the claim is citing Bricken et al. (2023) and SAE variants as background, so 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses'.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' central claim is that CircuitLasso matches intervention-based circuit discovery in structural accuracy at a fraction of the cost. They report that SAE-feature circuits are interpretable and useful for domain generalization. They state that the GPT-2 small propagation patterns characterize that model; whether they hold for more entangled SAE features remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pre-trained SAEs and observational sparse-regression circuit learning; it does not train or scale SAE dictionaries to study splitting.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper distinguishes dataset-level, prompt-averaged circuits from prompt-specific feature importance, but does not report that this changes any outcome relevant to the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Lasso-learned cross-layer circuits over GPT-2 small SAE features show qualitative persistence, merging, dropping, cause-effect and spurious associations between layer-wise features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in consecutive layers form traceable cross-layer paths in which semantic concepts persist, merge or narrow; this is a cross-layer analogue of feature refinement, distinct from dictionary-size splitting.

record.problems: The feature-circuit analysis is qualitative and conducted on GPT-2 small; semantic labels are assigned by inspection. The authors note possible spurious correlations and leave transfer to more entangled SAE features open. No dictionary-size sweep or split-specific coverage or geometry measures are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed versions were reported. Circuit benchmark SHD/runtime, CoLA faithfulness/completeness ablations, and Bias-in-Bios results were excluded because they evaluate circuit discovery or downstream prediction rather than SAE feature splitting.

untested.parts: All of it: no dictionary-size variation, input coverage or directional proximity.
All of it: open SAE releases (OpenAI GPT-2, Gemma Scope, Pythia) are used as tools only, with no splitting analysis.
All of it: no within-dictionary nested families or geometric closeness measured.
All of it: no parent/child firing analysis within an SAE, and no size or sparsity sweep of the SAE. The λ ablation varies the circuit Lasso penalty, not SAE sparsity.
All of it: no comparison across SAE sizes.
All of it: no alternative SAE objectives compared.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper never engages with feature splitting, only citing SAE work as background. Every row bears on no version, so their 'observed' states are reset to cannot_determine relative to the claim. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Dictionary-size scaling, replacement of coarse features by finer features, input coverage, and directional proximity.
Scaling or open-release testing of the splitting pattern.
Nested split families, geometric closeness, and correspondence to a concept hierarchy.
Parent-child split firing and whether changing SAE size or sparsity resolves absorption.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents and novel-latent comparisons.
Whether splitting results from the sparsity objective, or changes under alternative objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.size_stated: GPT-2 small; layer feature dictionary D = 32,768
rows.operation_detail: Traced semantically labeled SAE features across consecutive layers using learned adjacency matrices.
rows.measure: Persistence of a labeled semantic concept across the traced feature path
rows.value: The -self concept is identified in features 15186 (layer 8), 9592 (layer 9), 2985 (layer 10), 6368 (layer 11), and 20726 (layer 12).
rows.note: A qualitative cross-layer persistence observation, not a dictionary-size split or a geometric-distance measurement.
rows.check: Cross-layer persistence of '-self' across layer features at a fixed D=32,768. This is not a dictionary-size split. The 'observed' state bears on no version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.size_stated: GPT-2 small; layer feature dictionary D = 32,768
rows.operation_detail: Traced semantic parent features and child features across consecutive layers using learned adjacency matrices.
rows.measure: Semantic merging across a learned feature path
rows.value: Layer 9 feature 10609 is described as merging concepts from layer 8 features 15186 and 27170.
rows.note: The study describes a cross-layer circuit relationship, not multiple finer features replacing a coarse feature in a larger dictionary.
rows.check: Cross-layer 'merging' of two layer-8 features into one layer-9 feature. This is a circuit edge, not finer features replacing a coarse one within a dictionary. It bears on no version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.size_stated: GPT-2 small; layer feature dictionary D = 32,768
rows.operation_detail: Traced the semantic content of a feature across a learned consecutive-layer path.
rows.measure: Retention and dropping of semantic content across a feature path
rows.value: Layer 11 feature 6368 retains the “himself” concept and is described as disregarding other forms of -self represented by layer 10 feature 2985.
rows.note: This is a qualitative feature-transition observation, not a test of SAE absorption as defined in V4.
rows.check: A layer-11 feature keeps 'himself' and drops other '-self' forms seen in layer 10. This superficially resembles a parent/child relation, but it spans layers rather than SAE sizes. It is not absorption as V4 defines it (a parent failing to fire where a child takes over within one SAE).

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.size_stated: GPT-2 small; layer feature dictionary D = 32,768
rows.operation_detail: Examined semantic labels and direction of learned feature-circuit edges.
rows.measure: Reported semantic cause-effect association in the circuit
rows.value: Layer 9 feature 22314 is labeled hunger/thirst and is connected to layer 10 feature 5574 labeled ate/eat; the authors also note a path from layer 8 feature 1988 to layer 9 feature 22314 that appears anti-causal from a human perspective.
rows.note: The authors attribute the apparent anti-causal direction to their assumption that circuit direction follows model computation order.
rows.check: A cause-effect or anti-causal semantic edge between layers. Unrelated to splitting.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.size_stated: GPT-2 small; layer feature dictionary D = 32,768
rows.operation_detail: Examined semantic labels and learned feature-circuit associations.
rows.measure: Reported spurious semantic association in the learned circuit
rows.value: Layer 12 feature 20726, labeled -self, is described as spuriously correlated with layer 11 feature 29041, labeled hunger/thirst.
rows.note: The authors suggest training-data co-occurrence as a possible source of this association.
rows.check: A spurious cross-layer association. Unrelated to splitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
